newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
DENIS O'NEIL SCUTTLES CUP CHALLENGE

Australia's sole challenger for the 2000 America's Cup is now expected to be ocean racing veteran SYD FISCHER with his fifth bid to win the "Auld Mug" -- equalling SIR THOMAS LIPTON'S five challenges back in the 1920s and 1930s.
The Gazebo Hotel owner is expected to confirm his challenge early next week on the eve of the closing date of May 14 for challenges to be lodged with the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron.

This follows the shock decision by Sydney businessman and up-market property developer DENIS O'NEIL to scuttle the plan for he and yacht designer IAIN MURRAY to challenge through the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron.
The syndicate had planned a high profile announcement yesterday by New South Wales Premier BOB CARR at Government House but it was cancelled on Monday.

MURRAY, who skippered the America's Cup defender Kookaburra at Fremantle in 1987 and was one of the designers of the ill-fated oneAustralia at San Diego in 1995, told me that a challenge in New Zealand in 2000 had "all become too hard", adding that "all the fun has gone out of it".

MURRAY explained: "It's a combination of many things, the attitude of the New York Yacht Club, the difficulty in getting legal ownership of all the equipment from the oneAustralia challenge in 1995, and the huge cost of setting up a shore base on Auckland's waterfront."

The O'NEIL/MURRAY syndicate had purchased the oneAustralia equipment, including the second yacht sailed in the challenger eliminations in San Diego before the faster oneAustralia sank, together with spare masts, sails, shore-base equipment, and the performance and design computer software and records.

It had then found that ownership of all this vital equipment was tied up as security in Australian Federal Court proceedings against the oneAustralia syndicate headed by JOHN BERTRAND, Australia's winning skipper with Australia II at Newport, Rhode Island, in 1983.

On top of this major setback was dissatisfaction with the lack of progress with New Zealand's plans for a shore-base complex on Auckland Harbour -- at a cost double that which syndicates had paid in San Diego. On top of that, each syndicate would have to build all the infrastructure.
So far no challenger, nor indeed the defender, Team New Zealand, has signed up for a basic site at the waterfront complex.
Criticising the New Zealanders as "just money grabbers," MURRAY predicted that the total cost of several million dollars would force other challengers out of the America's Cup in 2000.
NORTEL'S BIG FUNDING FOR YACHTING

MURRAY, as a member of the board of the Australian Yachting Federation (AYF), was one of the many prominent sailors at the National Maritime Museum at Sydney's Darling Harbour for the announcement of a million dollar-plus sponsorship between the AYF and telecommunications company, Nortel.

The sponsorship, for the next four years, is the largest ever for Australian sailing and will support AYF activities from learn-to-sail programmes, coaching and development through club, state and national levels, organisation of Olympic-class events, and the training of Australian Olympic athletes for Sydney 2000 and beyond.
According to PHIL JONES, the recently-appointed AYF chief executive, the Nortel sponsorship will enable the Federation to accelerate its development plans for all levels of the sport.
"It is providing funds to develop sailing across the whole spectrum from beginner to Olympic standard," JONES said.
As part of the Nortel sponsorship, the AYF announced the members of the Australian Sailing Squad, 35 athletes who have qualified to train for the Sydney 2000 Olympics in eight classes.
Also announced were the eight teenage members of the Australian youth team heading off to Japan for the World Youth Championships in July.

The youth team includes brother and sister NATHAN and SARAH WILMOT, the children of Olympic and international yachtsman JAMIE WILMOT. NATHAN and SARAH will each helm a 420 dinghy at the World championships.
Also in the team is their cousin ROBBIE TREHARNE, son of America's Cup-winning tactician HUGH TREHARNE. ROBBIE will contest the boy's sailboard division of the world titles.
IAN BROWN APPOINTED HEAD COACH FOR 2000

One of the most significant announcements at the AYF function was that of the appointment of Olympic sailor and bronze medallist IAN BROWN as the federation's head coach for the Sydney 2000 Olympic campaign.

BROWN has been involved as an Olympic classes coach in recent years and has wide experience as an internationally-competitive sailor and one-time sailmaker. He was chosen from 20 applicants from Australia and overseas.

BROWN won the bronze medal in the 470 dinghy class at the Montreal Olympics and has been a top sailor in the Etchells class in recent years. In his role of head coach he will be responsible for allocating coaches to specific Olympic classes.
Also announced was the appointment of well-known yachtswoman TRACY JOHNSTON as the AYF's high-performance manager.
Johnston's task will be to look after all administrative aspects of the Olympic effort, including funding, international campaign programs and to be the contact with various Olympic bodies.
She is well equipped for this job, having held a senior administrative role with the Australian Olympic Committee before joining the AYF.
SNOW IN THE SOLOMONS
Not really! But Sydney yachtsman and director of Capital Properties GEORGE SNOW is not letting the seagrass grow under his keel while waiting for a new mast for his maxi yacht Brindabella.
He is heading to the Solomon Islands as skipper of the cruiser/racer Infinity III, a Beneteau-45, in the race through the Coral Sea from Brisbane to Gizo starting on May 17.

This is the second annual race to Gizo, run by the Royal Queensland Yacht Squadron and sponsored by Solomon Airways and the Gizo Hotel, and has attracted 20 racing and cruising entries from Australia and New Zealand.
In addition to SNOW with Infinity III, the racing division yachts include Let's Go Collex Onyx skippered by Lake Macquarie yachtsman ALYN OVENDEN and Sweet Caroline skippered by BILL RAWSON.
Race director, prominent Brisbane barrister DAYLE SMITH, is sailing his much-travelled Overdraft in the cruising division.
FLEET HEADING FOR PORT MORESBY
Another fleet of 21 monohull and multihull yachts is already heading for the tropics, with the Cairns-to-Port Moresby leg of the Shell Coral Sea Classic getting under way last Tuesday.
At last report, the multihull Gotcha Covered held a narrow lead from BZW Challenge, Nakari and More Bar Talk, sailing off the wind in moderate south-easterly tradewinds.

After two races of the Coral Sea Classic off the Queensland coast, More Bar Talk led the Performance Handicap (PHS) division for monohulls with 7.5 points (a first and a 7th) from BZW Challenge on 9.75 points (a 9th and a win).
Nakari led the multihull PHS division on 2.75 points from Gotcha Covered on 3.75 points.
E-MAIL OVER HF RADIO
Yet another an advance in marine communications! Penta Comstat VZX, that remarkable coastal marine station run by DEREK and JEANINE BARNARD, have introduced SeaMail -- e-mail over HF Radio.

SeaMail is a low-cost electronic mail message service for small craft. Connection with any e-mail address on the internet is now possible. All you need is an HF data modem with your existing HF radio and a PC. Penta Comstat VZX scans a range of data frequencies 24 hours a day.

Detailed information can be obtained from Penta Marine Radio Communications, PO Box 5149, Erina Fair 2250, by fax on 043 651494, e-mail pentacom ozemail.com.au or on the home page on the internet: http://www/ozemail.com.au/-pentacom
WINTER RACING AT RSYS

If you are finding the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia's Sunday Winter Series just too crowded with entries now exceeding 170 boats, the alternative could be the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron's Winter Series on Saturdays.
The racing starts on May 17 and runs through to August 2.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
